about: The Special Town Meeting on November 17, led by what residents care about (wallet, big, long-term, way of life): TC Passios, the track and field, the special education reserve, stormwater. Each line leaves its story on the site; the one dated action is the Finance Committee's public hearing. Figures from the board, recording figures only once checked by ear (heard-figures.csv).

text: Millions of dollars, and places people use every week, are on the line at Lunenburg's Special Town Meeting on {tm.date|day}. {tm.counts.on_warrant|n} questions are on the warrant so far:

🏚️ Tear down TC Passios? A non-binding question to voters. The building loses heat this winter and the food pantry is planning to move out. A building committee member put demolition at {tcp.heard[0].figure}.

🏟️ {trk.heard[0].figure} to engineer the Middle/High School track and field, the first step toward a project estimated at {trk.heard[1].figure}. The Select Board held it off the warrant at first, then put it on unanimously two weeks later. What changed?
🎒 {sped.heard[0].figure} from free cash for the special education reserve.

💧 Stormwater: a new fee, or the town budget? A non-binding vote. As the Stormwater Task Force presented it to the Select Board, the program costs about {sw.heard[0].figure} a year. Paid through property taxes, a typical home would pay about {sw.heard[1].figure} a year; under a separate stormwater fee, {sw.heard[2].figure}, with businesses and big parking lots paying more. Nothing has been voted. A second article lets the Planning Board set stormwater permit fees.
…plus the FY27 budget, corrective zoning and a bill from a prior year. The Select Board kept {tm.counts.kept_off|n} other articles off.
